*Chapter 1 finale. Played 2026-05-23.*
**Present:** Heidi ([[Characters/Anakis|Anakis]]), Caius ([[Characters/Arjun|Arjun]]), Brice ([[Characters/Quix|Quix]]), Dominic ([[Characters/Korvara Starglade|Korvara]]).
**Absent:** Cala ([[Characters/Freya|Freya]] — sick in real life and in-fiction, bunked below decks; [[Characters/Tariq|Tariq]] nursing her).
**Retired:** David ([[Characters/Dendrobo|Dendrobo]], gone since Session 4).

> **How the table diverged from the prep (read first):** The prepped three-way faction brawl never happened — Anakis talked the Zhentarim off the board before a shot was fired, and the Grey Hands snipers / Kiria / Yadira never appeared. The duel played as Charles arriving *himself* (no Simulacrum ice-decoy twist this session). The demiplane reveal happened **off-world** — Charles teleported the crew to a cathedral-lab on a nameless different planet, which is now the canonical home of CFAR's Mythallar vault (gods can't reach across the phlogiston; Faeressar was only a transfer point). The full Subject Zero / death-row reveal was given in the open. The detailed inspection-rack beats (BALDUR'S GATE chest, Subject Zero cabinet, Tessa) were *not* reached — moved to [[Unused Material]] for a future off-world session.

### Smell on the Wind
Half an hour before the midnight handoff. The decoy chest — packed with the modified cobalt crystals — sat strapped in the rowboat, humming wrong. Korvara and Arjun both caught it on an arcana/nature read: ozone and sickly-sweet decay, faint and everywhere at once, coming from nowhere. Arjun recognized it — *the smell from his Wall of the Faithless dream*, the wizard's signature. Korvara: "The stars are off. Something's unbalanced." A group religion check unlocked the cosmology lesson for the table: gods claim the souls of their worshippers; the **faithless** are condemned to the **Wall of the Faithless** in the **Fugue Plane**. Arjun is faithless — which is why Brother Valdris asked. Quix gave Tariq a quick shooting lesson before they shoved off. Korvara cast Guidance.

### The Rooftop Bluff
Anakis stealthed (23) onto the warehouse roof to overwatch the drop — and found **three Zhentarim** already there, set to ambush the handoff (the same outfit from Session 1). She snuck up behind them and flashed the **second-in-command's badge** looted in Session 2. Deception 18. The big one's eyes went wide and he bought it instantly; when his two subordinates balked, he *slashed one across the shoulder* — "Do not question me!" — and marched all three off the roof. One whole faction removed before initiative. *(GM aside at the table: "She upranked them" — the badge worked because they thought it meant she had authority over them. A third of the planned encounter deleted by one bluff.)*

### The Handoff & The Sphere
Emi played her part badly but sincerely — "You're the captain?" — and took the decoy at the green lantern, telling the crew their pay would come to the ship by dawn. The crew rowed ~90 ft down the canal and doubled back on foot. Ressik and two Returned loyalists crept in, told Emi her work was done ("report the cargo lost, no harm will come to you"), and Emi bolted. Ressik knelt and unlatched the chest. **The warehouse vaporized** — a perfect sphere of ash, the wood and "the fleshy parts" gone, the stone and canal mostly intact, water flashing to steam and rushing back. The whole city woke to the flash. The two loyalists were killed; **Ressik, half-orc-tanky, survived — unconscious, maybe dying.** Emi was knocked flat by the concussion.

### Grey Robes for Emi
Anakis (Perception 21) spotted **three grey-robed Church of Kelemvor figures** break from a nearby building, one shouting "You two handle the others — I'll get the woman," making straight for the dazed Emi. Initiative. The crew couldn't let Emi die (she's their payment and their cover). Korvara opened with Produce Flame (nat-ish 21 to hit) and dropped one — "they're crispy." Outgunned and outnumbered now, the lead Kelemvorite read the room and fled. *(These were run as CR 1/8 mooks at the table — generic clergy, not the prepped Yadira delegation.)* With the Kelemvorites scattering, Anakis moved inside to execute the unconscious Ressik — the Returned leader couldn't be left alive with Emi's family in the balance. Quix and Korvara flagged the moral weight of finishing an unconscious prisoner; Anakis didn't flinch.

### "Where Is Arjun? I Have Words For Him."
As Anakis closed on Ressik, the rot-and-ozone smell crashed over the scene, gag-inducing now even to those who'd only sensed it faintly. Ressik's lips moved and **a voice that was not hers, layered with a thousand voices**, said: *"Thank you for trying to return this one to me, but I'm afraid I have other plans for her."* A **vertical tear ripped open** above her body, fog billowing out, and a **decrepit old man** stepped through, walked over Ressik, and asked for Arjun.

Caius's moment: Arjun asked the man's name, then **shot him clean through the forehead** (17 to hit). The old man froze, fell, lay dead — **and stood back up,** shaking his head. *"That wasn't very nice. I thought I was being polite."* His eyes cycled **black to white to grey.** This was Magnus, the wizard Arjun has chased for years — **functionally immortal.** He gestured Ressik's limp body into the air to float behind him, snapped his fingers, and **four corpses rose as zombies.** Arjun emptied back to the crew. Anakis sprinted to break **Emi's distress twig** — the signal to the CFAR tower.

### Charles Comes Himself
The horizon pulled like a curtain — space folded, the distant blue spire of CFAR warped to a few feet away, and **Charles yn Hakim el Xander** stepped out of a door in the air. He and Magnus locked eyes. Magnus leered: *"I bet you didn't think you'd see me again, after sending me where you sent me."* Charles raised a hand and loosed a **massive lightning bolt** — which **sank into Magnus's body and did nothing.** The two archmages went at it (narrated above the action) while the crew dealt with the zombies: Quix and Arjun chipping shamblers down, Korvara and Anakis holding the line, a couple of hits landed (Korvara took 7 bludgeoning). Charles, wounded, eventually drove Magnus back. Magnus **retreated into the rift to the Fugue Plane** — the place he now calls home, able to come and go through the tear. Charles drank a potion (bones audibly resetting), spat blood, and **levitated over to the crew, "not doing so hot"** but alive. *"Don't waste your magic on me. I'll be fine. I've had worse."*

### The Off-World Cathedral
Charles paid the crew their fee (pouch tossed to Arjun, the captain). He asked Anakis to audit the rest of his chests — his detection spells had caught her repairing the housing en route, and the fault was something he'd "personally missed." The crew tried to walk ("we did the job, we're done") until he sweetened it: **the orphanage covered — negotiated up from six months to a full year, all equipment refreshed.** Then he gathered them, reached for something in a dimension they couldn't see, and **pulled them off the planet entirely** — stars streaking past — onto **a nameless different world.**

A **cathedral-scale arcane laboratory:** researchers at screens and clipboards, anti-scrying enchantments flaring underfoot at the threshold, and behind a side door an **arbitrarily-large warehouse of Mythallars** — rows on rows on rows of the device they'd carried one of. *"Gods cannot reach through the phlogiston of space,"* Charles explained; that's why the base is off-world and **deliberately nameless** ("Don't name it, for god's sake — it makes it harder to be scried"). *(Aside: he flies back yearly to re-kill a weakened goddess who keeps trying to lock Icewind Dale in eternal winter. "Not important.")*

### The Confession (Subject Zero, in the open)
Charles came clean: *"I wasn't really hiring you to transport the Mythallar. I was hiring you to be bait for Magnus."* Arjun, dry: "Well, that worked out — I was hunting him anyway." Charles: *"But he was hunting you."* The full truth, laid out:
- Calimport still executes its most violent criminals. Charles offers the condemned a deal: **resurrection under experimental conditions.** Survive intact and it counts as time served. Most don't survive intact.
- **Magnus murdered an entire family**, deliberately luring them *outside the death-detection network* so the EMTs couldn't revive them. He was sentenced to death and **took the experimental-resurrection deal — he is Subject Zero.**
- The experiment: how far into the Fugue Plane can you send a soul and pull it back. Charles sent Magnus **further than any mortal has ever gone — beyond the Wall of the Faithless,** into unventured territory. There Magnus *"encountered something. Very powerful. Very angry with me and the things I'm doing. Invested in the cycle of souls — and malevolent. It found a kindred spirit in Magnus and empowered him the way only the chosen of a god are empowered."*
- Magnus came back **wrathful and beyond Charles's control, and escaped.** He still holds **Arjun's captive friend hidden somewhere — Charles couldn't locate them, "hidden from scrying as well."**
- Charles believes **the gods themselves have now taken notice of CFAR** — which is why the war just got much harder, and why the base sits off-world.
- Asked outright, Charles admitted **he is faithless too:** *"I do not see the gods as ethical. I believe they are tyrants exploiting the mortal realm for their own benefit, and that they are too powerful to be allowed to exist."* (A mirror of Arjun.)

### The Deal & The Lift-Off
Charles offered an ongoing arrangement: **protection** (the crew is now on Magnus's radar) and **lucrative paid missions** in exchange for aligning with CFAR's goals — starting with auditing/repairing the chest fault so no other housing cascades the way theirs did. Future missions would often come via his **Simulacrum** (all equally strong, each with an implanted sending stone so he can monitor). The crew **took the money and the implied arrangement without signing onto anything** — CFAR-aligned by default, free to walk. Charles, with a research center, a city, gods, and "many cosmic catastrophes" to manage, handed them off to Emi for the details and left. **Everyone leveled to 3.**

## Loot & Rewards
- Delivery fee paid in full (per-crew, handed to Arjun as captain).
- **Anakis's orphanage in Baldur's Gate: refurbished + fully funded for 12 months**, all equipment refreshed (negotiated up from Charles's opening offer of 6).
- Standing offer from Charles: protection + paid CFAR missions (tentatively accepted, nothing signed).
- **Level 3.**

## Quotes
- Magnus (through Ressik): *"Thank you for trying to return this one to me, but I'm afraid I have other plans for her."*
- Magnus, after taking a bullet through the skull and standing back up: *"That wasn't very nice. I thought I was being polite."*
- Magnus to Charles: *"I bet you didn't think you'd see me again, after sending me where you sent me."*
- Arjun, on learning he was bait: *"Well, that worked out — I was hunting Magnus anyway."* / Charles: *"But he was hunting you."*
- Charles: *"Gods cannot reach through the phlogiston of space."* / *"Don't name it, for god's sake."*
- Charles, on the gods: *"They are tyrants... too powerful to be allowed to exist."*
- Anakis, weighing executing the unconscious Ressik: *"I don't see the moral issue."*

## Scenes Not Reached (→ moved to [[Unused Material]])
- The prepped **three-way faction chaos** at Slip 14 (Grey Hands snipers, Kiria Shadowmend's Zhentarim cell, Yadira al-Hakam's Kelemvorite delegation, the axes/redirect mechanics, all statblocks). None of these specific NPCs appeared.
- The **Simulacrum "ice and snow" two-wizard duel** choreography (Charles came himself; the decoy-corpse twist is unused and can be deployed in a future Charles/Vell clash).
- The **inspection-rack reveal**: the twelve city-name chests (BALDUR'S GATE etc.), the gold-filament fault on multiple chests, **Tessa's** handwriting matching Anakis's, **Vorm**, and the sealed **SUBJECT ZERO cabinet**. Relocate this scene to the off-world cathedral for when Anakis returns to audit the chests.
- **Lira's Harper bird / note** to Korvara — not delivered; carry into Chapter 2.
- Korvara catching the **red (Bhaal) eye-flicker** and the "more than three" hint — only black/white/grey shown; save the full Five reveal for Chapter 2.

The wizard [[Characters/Arjun|Arjun]] has hunted for years. Appears as a **decrepit old man**; scarred lip (Arjun threw a knife years ago). **Eyes cycle black → white → grey** (the three death-gods; see [[Campaign Reference doc]] "The Five"). Aura of rot-and-ozone that bleeds into the world ahead of him — the smell from Arjun's Wall of the Faithless dream.

**True identity:** **SUBJECT ZERO** — [[Characters/Charles Xander|Charles]]'s first and worst experimental-resurrection subject. A convicted murderer (slaughtered an entire family, deliberately luring them *outside* the death-detection network so they couldn't be revived). Condemned to death by Calimport courts; took CFAR's standing death-row resurrection deal. Charles sent him **further into the Fugue Plane than any mortal has gone — beyond the Wall of the Faithless** — where he encountered "something very powerful, very angry, invested in the cycle of souls, and malevolent," which empowered him like a god's chosen. Came back wrathful, uncontrollable, escaped.

**Pre-mortem:** high-functioning psychopath. Enchanted Arjun's friend off a shared job and took them captive; Arjun scarred his lip throwing a knife. **He still holds that friend somewhere, hidden from scrying** — even Charles can't locate them.

**Post-resurrection:** **functionally immortal** — Arjun shot him through the forehead (S5), he dropped dead, then stood back up unharmed. Believes he *seized* his power in the Fugue Plane on his own merit; **does not know the Five exist** or that he is, theologically, the Dead Three's newest member-in-waiting. This delusion makes him effective for them — no theological hesitation.

**Powers seen (S5):** opens a vertical Fugue rift and walks through walls/space; speaks **through the bodies of the Returned** in a thousand-layered voice; **un-resurrects / claims the Returned** (carried Ressik off beyond the Wall — no body); **raises the recent dead as zombies** with a snap; **absorbs spell energy** (Charles's lightning bolt sank into him and did nothing). Comes and goes through the Fugue Plane, which he now calls home.

**What he wants:** **Arjun.** He came to Faeressar specifically for "words" with the only mortal who can identify him on sight and who once made him afraid. Secondary: the Mythallar / CFAR infrastructure.

## Session Log
- **S1–S3 (background):** Arjun's betrayer; trail went cold in Calimport where the crew heard he'd "died and been resurrected." Appears in Arjun's S3 Wall-of-the-Faithless dream (color-shifting eyes).
- **S5:** Manifested at Slip 14 through Ressik's body, stepped out as the old man, asked for Arjun. Survived a point-blank headshot. Raised four zombies. Dueled Charles, shrugged off a lightning bolt, was eventually driven back and **retreated into the Fugue rift.** Left holding the question of Arjun's captive friend. *"You will see me again."*

## Open Threads
- Where is Arjun's captive friend? Magnus has them hidden from scrying.
- What did he encounter beyond the Wall? (The Five — full reveal saved for Ch 2.)
- He can un-resurrect *any* Returned → every member of [[Demos Twice-Fallen]]'s movement is potential fuel.
- He doesn't know he's the gods' tool, not a self-made god. Disabusing him (or not) is a lever.

Full encounter is preserved in `Session 5 prep.md` ("Monsters / Encounters"). Reusable as a future contested-objective fight anywhere a MacGuffin is in play. Includes complete statblocks for:

- **Doomguide Acolytes Petros & Tomé** — Petros (young, scared, first time off temple grounds, turnable into an info source with one kind word) and Tomé (old, calm, administers last rites mid-combat).

## The Simulacrum "Ice and Snow" Duel
The cinematic two-wizard choreography where Charles's first body is killed by Vell, **shatters into snow** (Simulacrum decoy), and the *real* Charles drops from above. Charles came himself in S5, so this is **unused** — deploy at a future Charles/Magnus clash, or retroactively reveal that the wounded Charles the crew met was watching through an implanted sending stone. I will not be."*

- **Vorm** (dwarf arcanist, spectacles, calipers) — the engineer who just watched his boss nearly die.
- The sealed **SUBJECT ZERO cabinet** — lead, Doomguide writ, "DO NOT RESURRECT, 1481 DR." (Now partly explained by Charles's open confession, but the *physical cabinet* and what's still in it remain a beat. Note: Subject Zero = Magnus, now loose — so what's in the cabinet? An empty cell? A second subject?)

input.content:
*Living document. Drafted end of Chapter 1 (post-Session 5). Hold loosely — this is a map of situations and a target shape, not a railroad.*
# The Calimport Campaign — Arc Plan

## The Story We're Telling

> **A campaign about grief and the temptation to undo a loss — set inside a war over whether death, and the gods who rule it, should be allowed to exist at all.**

Strip away the Mythallar and the factions and the engine underneath is this: **every one of these five carries a specific death they couldn't prevent.** Arjun's cellmates at the broken bridge. Quix's Olivea, because he reached for the loot instead of her hand. Korvara's crash comrades, whom she ran from. Anakis's orphans, left behind. Freya's debt, which will force her to betray people who trust her. And [[Factions/CFAR|CFAR]] has invented the one thing each of them secretly wishes they'd had: **a way to bring back the person they couldn't save.**

So the macro plot is a mirror of the micro wound. Whatever the crew decides about resurrection, they're really deciding about their own dead.

**What Session 5 added — the cosmic axis.** [[Characters/Charles Xander|Charles]] isn't only fighting death; he's **faithless**, and he's fighting *the gods themselves* — "tyrants exploiting the mortal realm, too powerful to be allowed to exist." The gods answered by reaching through his own experiment, past the Wall of the Faithless, to empower **[[Characters/Magnus Vell|Magnus]] (Subject Zero)** as their counterweight — a monster who doesn't know he's a tool. The crew has now **tentatively signed on with the faithless utopian who used them as bait.**

**Why this is personal for the captain:** [[Characters/Arjun|Arjun]] is faithless too. If he dies unclaimed, **the Wall of the Faithless is literally his fate** — and the one man who can send him there, Magnus, is holding a friend of his captive. Arjun is hunting the thing that can damn him, to free someone he already failed once. That's the whole campaign in one character.

**The finale question:** *Should death be optional? Should the gods be broken to make it so? And when each of these five is offered their own dead back — at the cost of feeding the machine that may end the cycle of souls — what do they choose?* The crew ends up brokering that answer because they're the only faction with a foot in every camp: a faithless captain, a CFAR patron, a Harper spy, a Broker mole, and a woman who runs an orphanage.

---

## The Arc Map (Chapters 2–6)

Sized for first-time players incl. Caius (9). Currently **level 3**. Target: ~level 11–13 by the finale. Each chapter ≈ 4–6 sessions; hold the count loosely.

### Chapter 2 — "On Our Terms" *(the alignment chapter)*
**Premise:** Back to Calimport with a patron for the first time. The owed conversation with Charles ("your timing, your terms"). The crew runs its first real CFAR jobs — paid, often briefed by a [[Characters/Charles Xander|Charles]] **Simulacrum**. They finally see the city as players, not couriers. Anakis cashes in her standing task: the **chest-fault audit at the off-world base**, which pays off the unrevealed inspection-rack beats (the twelve city-name chests, **BALDUR'S GATE**, **Tessa**, the sealed **SUBJECT ZERO cabinet** — see [[Unused Material]]). The crew learns the *scale*: thousands of faulty chests = thousands of bombs in transit, and the engineer is one of the only people alive who can spot the fault.
**Spotlight:** the crew defines what "tentatively aligned" actually costs. **Korvara's** [[Characters/Lira|Lira]] Harper-bird lands — spy on the patron you just joined. **Anakis** sits in the contradiction (her kids stop dying *and* the rack is endless).
**Threads retired/advanced:** the owed Charles conversation; Korvara's Harper recruitment goes live; the chest-fault stakes; first crack in the "tentative" alignment.
**Ends on:** a wedge that makes neutrality impossible — a CFAR job that asks the crew to do something they don't like.

### Chapter 3 — "Little Keeper of the Quiet Sun" *(the descent)*
**Premise:** The [[Characters/CM-7|CM-7]] + Netherese thread becomes a proper adventure arc. Recover CM-7's scattered body from the **sunken Netherese city** (marked Session 2) and Synod ruins. Arjun's companion finally wakes and *chooses* him. The lore floor drops out: **Netheril already built resurrection/Mythallar tech — and fell.** The cautionary precedent for everything Charles is doing. Possible first physical lead on **Arjun's captive friend** (Magnus haunts Fugue-adjacent, Netherese-flavored places).
**Spotlight:** **Arjun + CM-7.** A dungeon-flavored chapter — the young player gets a companion payoff and clear "Captain, what do you do?" beats. Power-up chapter.
**Threads retired/advanced:** CM-7 restoration (partial); Netherese cautionary lore; the Mythallar's true cost; a thread toward the captive friend.

### Chapter 4 — "The Wall Is Personal" *(the counterweight & the friend)*
**Premise:** [[Characters/Magnus Vell|Magnus]] returns as an active force and the hunt for Arjun's friend goes hot. The campaign refuses to let Magnus be a flat villain: the **Five reveal** lands (he's the gods' weapon and doesn't know it; he was *used*, exactly like the crew was). He can **un-resurrect the Returned** — so [[Characters/Demos Twice-Fallen|Demos]]'s whole movement is now prey, and that grief/terror is a faction in motion. Running underneath: **Quix's** arc made literal — Olivea, the McToad brothers, Crimmor. Does undoing a death feed Magnus and the cosmic machine? Would Quix take the do-over if it did?
**Spotlight:** **Arjun + Quix.** The personal cost of cheating death, dramatized twice.
**Threads retired/advanced:** the Five revealed; the captive friend located/confronted; Demos & the Returned in crisis; Quix's grief arc.

### Chapter 5 — "Tyrants" *(the god war)*
**Premise:** Charles's real endgame surfaces — not just beating death but **breaking the gods' grip and dismantling the Wall of the Faithless.** The **Mandate's** maximalist push (CFAR everywhere, no opt-out, now) collides with **Seraphina's** apocalyptic vision (the Fugue Plane emptying, death-gods withering, the barrier between life and death collapsing). The gods escalate through Magnus and others. The crew is now deep enough inside CFAR to be the swing vote nobody planned for.
**Spotlight:** **Korvara + Freya.** The Harper (a city run on one man's control of death is too much power) and the [[Characters/The Broker|Broker]]'s mole (Ruin-aligned: burn it all) both have to choose the crew over their handlers.
**Threads retired/advanced:** the Mandate; Seraphina's vision; Freya's debt & the Broker's true agenda; Korvara's loyalty test; the gods as active antagonists.

### Chapter 6 — "Death, Made Optional" *(the settlement)*
**Premise:** Finale. Each PC is offered their dead back, **on screen, with a price** — Arjun's cellmates and friend, Quix's Olivea, Korvara's crash comrades, the kids Anakis lost, the death behind Freya's debt. They choose. Then the crew — the only faction *everyone* half-trusts — brokers a settlement between Charles, the Church, the gods, and Magnus. Not "destroy CFAR" or "save CFAR." **Terms:** whether and how death can be cheated, and whether the Wall stands. **Arjun's captain's-call closes the campaign the way it opened — bait who became the man who decided.**
**Spotlight:** all five at once (by design, the same question asked five ways converges here).

---

## Per-PC Throughline (so nobody gets dropped)

| PC (player) | Their question | Primary payoff |
|---|---|---|
| **[[Characters/Arjun\|Arjun]]** (Caius) | Will you face the thing that can damn you, to save the friend you failed — and what does a faithless captain owe the dead? | Ch 3 (CM-7), Ch 4, Ch 6 |
| **[[Characters/Anakis\|Anakis]]** (Heidi) | Is scaling this safe — and who pays when it isn't? Every city is your city for somebody. | Ch 2 (the rack), Ch 5 |
| **[[Characters/Quix\|Quix]]** (Brice) | If you could reach for Olivea's hand again, would you — even knowing what it feeds? | Ch 4 |
| **[[Characters/Korvara Starglade\|Korvara]]** (Dominic) | Is one faithless man controlling death worth betraying the crew you just joined to stop? | Ch 2 (Harper), Ch 5 |
| **[[Characters/Freya\|Freya]]** (Cala) | When the Broker's real agenda surfaces — burn it all — whose side are you on? | Ch 5 |

The design payoff: these are the **same question asked five ways**, so the Chapter 6 "undo your loss?" choice lands for everyone simultaneously.

---

## Principles to Preserve (from the Reference doc, carried forward)

- **Moral complexity over villains.** Charles used the crew and is half-right. Magnus is a monster *and* a victim. The Church is correct that this could end the world. The Returned are dying and impatient and not wrong.
- **Age-appropriate for Caius.** Keep giving Arjun clear "Captain, what do you do?" hero beats and a companion (CM-7). Violence stays heroic, not grim.
- **Firearms standard; factor into CR.** Encounters built on the [[Campaign Reference doc|Axes method]], not just "hit the bad guys."
- **The crew is the seam.** Their power isn't levels — it's that they're the only people with a foot in every camp. The finale should *only* be solvable by people positioned exactly as they are.

---

# Lazy Campaign Building Checklist

## Initial Campaign Planning
1. **Choose an RPG system** – Select your game mechanics foundation
2. **Choose a campaign setting** – Determine your world
3. **Conduct informal conversations with players** – "get buy in" before committing to your choices

## Pre-Session Zero Campaign Prep
4. **Develop your campaign's hook** – Establish what draws players in
5. **Establish campaign truths** – Define foundational facts about your world
6. **Prepare worldbuilding questions** – "Focus these questions on the things you actually want answers to"
7. **Create a campaign one-pager** – Consolidate essential information

## Run Your Session Zero
8. **Review the campaign one-pager** – Present your foundation
9. **Discuss character bonds to theme** – Connect characters to campaign identity
10. **Discuss character bonds to each other** – Build party cohesion
11. **Optionally assign starting factions** – Give characters organizational ties
12. **Optionally answer worldbuilding questions** – Collaborate on world details
13. **Review Lines and Veils** – Establish safety boundaries
14. **Review "Pause for a Minute"** – Enable table safety tools
15. **Build characters together** – Collaborative character creation
16. **Run a short adventure** – Test mechanics and chemistry (optional)

## After Your Session Zero
17. **Embrace spiral campaign development** – Grow your world iteratively
18. **Flesh out starting location** – Build "locations they need to set them off on adventures and to recover"
19. **Prepare three quests** – Offer meaningful choices
20. **Use eight steps for future adventures** – Systematic prep methodology

## Develop the World
21. **Create three villains** – Establish antagonistic forces with goals
22. **Develop additional factions** – Create "one or two good, shady, and bad"
23. **Build practical pantheon** – Include religions characters encounter
24. **Establish practical history** – Provide discoverable lore
25. **Build faction list** – Create rollable options for flavor
26. **Utilize magic system and economy** – "Keep it simple"

## Key Overarching Principles
- **Focus on character-driven development:** Build details "important to the characters"
- **Spiral outward:** Start small and expand based on play
- **Simplicity:** "Keep things simple" and add complexity only as needed
- **Iterative growth:** "spiraling outwards" from character needs to larger world

# Summary of "Thinking Two Horizons Out"

## What Are the Horizons?

Sly Flourish describes two conceptual circles of awareness for campaign planning:

**First Horizon**: The immediate area around the characters—what they can see and reach right now. This includes the eight steps of lazy DM prep focused on the next session.

**Second Horizon**: Future locations and developments beyond the characters' current view. Rather than mapping 300+ square miles, Flourish suggests focusing on "three hexes out"—three interesting locations the party might explore next.

## Planning Distance

Flourish advises DMs to **think ahead to the second horizon** by identifying potential future adventures and dropping hints about them now. However, he explicitly warns against over-preparing distant content: "We don't need full maps of the locations or full rosters of monsters, NPCs, and treasure."

A key practical recommendation: "When possible, help players choose their next path at the end of a session to help you focus your prep on the path they chose." This prevents wasting preparation on options players never pursue.

## Prep Philosophy

Rather than locking in plots, Flourish emphasizes using the second horizon for **seeds and foreshadowing**—hints that can grow into actual adventures based on player choice. This spiral approach builds outward from character position, keeping prep flexible and player-driven.

# Calimport — Campaign One-Pager

## Hook (the pitch)
*A crew of broke smugglers in the largest city in Faerûn takes questionable jobs in a world where one man has made death optional — and keeps ending up holding the biggest questions in the realm.* (Firefly, but the cargo is resurrection.)

## The Six Truths
1. **Death is optional now — and it breaks everything.** [[Factions/CFAR|CFAR]]'s resurrection network means the powerful no longer fear death, the death-gods are being bypassed, and law, faith, and power are all in upheaval.
2. **The gods are real, present, and self-interested.** They claim the souls of their worshippers and condemn the **faithless** to the Wall of the Faithless. They are not kind. [[Characters/Charles Xander|Charles]] thinks they're tyrants who should be overthrown.
3. **One faithless man holds the lever.** Charles Xander — archmage, ruler of Calimport — controls the resurrection infrastructure and is scaling it across Faerûn from a base **off-world, beyond the gods' reach.**
4. **Everyone who can resurrect has enemies who can't.** The Church (death is sacred), the Zhentarim (assassination is pointless now), the Returned (impatient for more), and the **gods themselves** all push back.
5. **Netheril did this before, and Netheril fell.** The Mythallar and the tech are 3,000-year-old Netherese work. The precedent is a warning written in a sunken city.
6. **The crew are smugglers, not heroes** — and each is haunted by a death they couldn't stop. That guilt is the hook every big choice pulls on.

## The Three Villains *(as Sly Flourish "fronts" — goal + escalation)*
1. **[[Characters/Magnus Vell|Magnus Vell]] / Subject Zero** — *the gods' blade, personal to the captain.* **Goal:** take Arjun, finish what he started; (unknowingly) act as the gods' counterweight; consume the Returned. **Escalation:** un-resurrections rise → the Returned start vanishing → Arjun's captive friend used as bait → the Wall calls Arjun by name.
2. **The Mandate (CFAR overreach)** — *the danger of the cause the crew serves.* **Goal:** scale resurrection to all Faerûn, no opt-out, become the state. The villain is the overreach, not Charles. **Escalation:** faulty chests detonate in cities → opt-out criminalized → the off-world god-war escalates → Charles declines and the umbrella thins.
3. **The Ruin / [[Characters/The Broker|The Broker]]** — *the burn-it-all saboteurs.* **Goal:** destroy CFAR and Calimport rather than let one man own death; [[Characters/Freya|Freya]]'s handler. **Escalation:** sabotage → the Broker's web tightens → Freya's debt called in → an attempt to compromise the demiplane lattice.
> **Behind the curtain:** the Five (the death-gods + hidden Bane/Bhaal). The distant threat, expressed through Magnus. Full reveal saved for Chapter 2.

## Key NPCs
- **[[Characters/Charles Xander|Charles]]** — patron/antagonist; faithless; used the crew as bait; now wounded and owes them. The "dangerous good."
- **[[Characters/Magnus Vell|Magnus]]** — immortal, Fugue-empowered; holds Arjun's friend; hunts Arjun.
- **[[Characters/Emi Sandoval|Emi]]** — CFAR handler who kept the crew's cover; ally.
- **[[Characters/Lira|Lira]]** — Harper agent; wants Korvara to spy on CFAR.
- **[[Characters/Demos Twice-Fallen|Demos]]** — leader of the Returned; doesn't yet know Magnus took Ressik irreversibly.
- **[[Characters/Tariq|Tariq]]** — crew orphan, semi-adopted. **[[Characters/CM-7|CM-7]]** — broken Netherese construct bonded to Arjun.

## Factions (kept to the ones that touch the characters)
[[Factions/CFAR|CFAR]] (patron) · [[Factions/Church of Kelemvor|Church of Kelemvor]] (death is sacred) · [[Factions/The Zhentarim|Zhentarim]] (leverage; the Ruin cell) · [[Factions/The Returned|The Returned]] (resurrected radicals) · The Harpers (watchers of concentrated power). *(The full ~18-faction roster lives in `Factions/` — see "Method notes" in [[Campaign Arc Plan]] re: pruning.)*

## Where We Are (first horizon)
End of Chapter 1. **Level 3.** Tentatively CFAR-aligned (paid, unsigned). Charles wounded & grounded. Magnus loose. Anakis owes a chest-fault audit. Freya just back from being sick.

## Three Quests on Offer (second horizon — let the players pick at session's end)
1. **The Audit** *(Anakis-forward)* — return to the off-world base to inspect the faulty chests. *Mystery:* what's in the **Subject Zero cabinet** now that Subject Zero is loose?
2. **The Harper Meet** *(Korvara-forward)* — answer [[Characters/Lira|Lira]]'s summons and get pulled into spying on the patron they just joined.
3. **The Captive Friend** *(Arjun-forward)* — chase the first lead on Arjun's imprisoned friend, putting the crew back on Magnus's radar.
> **Lurking complication (can intrude on any path):** [[Characters/Demos Twice-Fallen|Demos]] and the grieving Returned come looking for the crew that baited Ressik.

## The method, analyzed

Sly Flourish's [Lazy Campaign Building Checklist](https://slyflourish.com/lazy_campaign_building_checklist.html) is a **different framework from his session-prep eight steps**, and it runs in three phases:

1. **Initial planning** — system, setting, informal player buy-in *before* you commit.
2. **Pre–Session Zero** — develop the **hook**, establish a few **campaign "truths"** (foundational world-facts), prep worldbuilding questions, and write a **one-page campaign sheet**.
3. **Session Zero + spiral development** — review the one-pager, build **character bonds to the theme and to each other**, set safety tools (Lines & Veils), then *after* Session Zero **"spiral outward"**: flesh out only the starting location, offer **three quests**, and use the eight steps for each next adventure. World-development (three villains, a few factions, practical pantheon/history) comes **as you need it.**

The load-bearing philosophy underneath it all: **prep situations, not plots.** He frames prep as "dishes of pre-cooked food to improvise the meal at the table," not a story you build in advance. And his [Thinking Two Horizons Out](https://slyflourish.com/thinking_two_horizons_out.html) essay is explicit: plan the next session firmly, sketch a *handful* of possible next destinations as **seeds to foreshadow**, and **let players choose their path at session's end** so you never over-prep distant content.

## The one tension worth naming

Your instinct last turn — *"plan the remainder of the arcs"* — runs slightly against the grain of the method, which says **don't plot the campaign; spiral two horizons out.** The good news is they reconcile cleanly: keep the six-chapter arc as a **thematic North Star + thread tracker**, but only *firm-prep Chapter 2* and let the players' choices redraw 3 onward. I wrote that reconciliation into the top of the Arc Plan so the doc doesn't read as a railroad.

## What I applied (three artifacts in the campaign folder)

- **`Lazy Campaign Sheet.md`** — his signature one-pager for Calimport: the **Hook**, **Six Truths**, **three villain "fronts"** (Magnus / the Mandate / the Ruin-Broker, with escalation clocks), the live NPCs and factions, and **three quests on offer** for Chapter 2 (the Audit / the Harper Meet / the Captive Friend) so the players can pick at session's end.
- **`Campaign Arc Plan.md`** — added the "two horizons out" framing up top + a **Method Notes** section mapping the campaign against his checklist.
- Both lean on the **Six Truths** and **villain fronts**, which the campaign had implicitly but never stated.

## Genuine gaps the method surfaced

1. **Lines & Veils — worth one quick chat with Heidi.** The checklist puts safety tools in Session Zero, and it matters more here because **Caius is 9** and Session 5 got dark (a murdered family, the body-horror Wall, a person dragged past it). You have an implicit "age-appropriate for Caius" rule; making it explicit before the Ch-2 cosmic horror deepens is low-effort, high-value.
2. **Character bonds to *each other* are thin.** The crew is bonded by circumstance and shared guilt, but not to one another. Cala/Freya returning is a natural moment to seed a private history or debt between two PCs.
3. **Faction sprawl.** ~18 faction notes is the opposite of "lazy / build only what you need." Not a problem if you enjoy it (you clearly do), but the method would prune active prep to the ~5 that touch the characters and treat the rest as a rollable flavor list. The one-pager already does that pruning.

Want me to turn the **three Chapter 2 quests into a proper Session 6 prep** once you know which the players lean toward — or run the **Lines & Veils** conversation framing for Heidi first?

Sources: [Lazy Campaign Building Checklist](https://slyflourish.com/lazy_campaign_building_checklist.html) · [Thinking Two Horizons Out](https://slyflourish.com/thinking_two_horizons_out.html) · [The Eight Steps – 2023 Review](https://slyflourish.com/eight_steps_2023.html)

Verification's back — my read of the method holds up, with one correction worth making since I already said it out loud:

**Correction:** I fused two of his ideas into one. The *"pre-cooked dishes, improvise the meal"* metaphor is specifically about his **eight-step session prep** — whereas **"situations, not plots"** is a *separate* named concept with its own checklist. They're complementary, but two different articles, not one framing.

That separate concept is actually a useful bonus tool for us. Sly Flourish's **[Situation Checklist](https://slyflourish.com/situation_checklist.html)** says to build each adventure node as four things instead of a plot:

> **Location · Inhabitants · Goal · Complications** — *"There's no plot. There's no expected path. There's no single ending."*

That's a cleaner way to express the three Chapter 2 quests on the one-pager. Right now they're written as quest *pitches*; reframing each as a situation makes them improv-ready and removes any implied "correct path." For example:

- **The Audit** → *Location:* the off-world vault. *Inhabitants:* Tessa (ally), Vorm (rattled), a Simulacrum of Charles. *Goal:* audit the faulty chests. *Complications:* the Subject Zero cabinet is open/empty; the fault rate is worse than Charles admitted; Tessa wants to defect.

Two smaller notes from the check, for the record: **"Six Truths"** is his canonical label but the count is explicitly flexible (3–7), and he stresses truths ≠ secrets/clues — ours are correctly truths. Everything else confirmed against primary sources.

## Three Situations on Offer (second horizon — let the players pick at session's end)
*Built as Sly Flourish [situations](https://slyflourish.com/situation_checklist.html), not plots: Location · Inhabitants · Goal · Complications. No expected path, no single ending.*

### 1. The Audit *(Anakis-forward)*
- **Location:** the nameless **off-world vault** — cathedral-scale lab, anti-scrying threshold, the arbitrarily-large Mythallar rack; the twelve city-name chests on the inspection bench (BALDUR'S GATE among them).
- **Inhabitants:** **[[Characters/Tessa|Tessa]]** (researcher whose warnings went unheard; wants out), **Vorm** (rattled dwarf arcanist), a **Charles Simulacrum** (helpful, deflecting), warehouse staff.
- **Goal:** audit and repair the gold-filament fault before more chests detonate in transit.
- **Complications:** the **Subject Zero cabinet is open / empty** (where is what was in it?); the real fault rate is far worse than Charles admitted; Tessa's diagnostic notes match Anakis's handwriting and she quietly asks for help defecting; the Simulacrum is *monitoring* via its sending stone.

### 2. The Harper Meet *(Korvara-forward)*
- **Location:** a Faeressar back-room or a Calimport safehouse — wherever **[[Characters/Lira|Lira]]**'s bird leads.
- **Inhabitants:** **[[Characters/Lira|Lira]]** (Harper handler), possibly **Firros** (Korvara's old contact), a Harper cell wary of CFAR.
- **Goal:** the Harpers want eyes inside CFAR — they see one faithless man controlling death across Faerûn as a catastrophic concentration of power.
- **Complications:** the crew **just took CFAR's coin** — this is spying on a patron mid-handshake; the ask escalates (pass a message → copy a manifest → plant a device); Charles's Simulacrum could be watching any meeting; the rest of the crew may not agree to it.

### 3. The Captive Friend *(Arjun-forward)*
- **Location:** the first **lead on Arjun's imprisoned friend** — a Crimmor contact, a Fugue-touched ruin, or a name Magnus left behind.
- **Inhabitants:** an informant who knew the friend, low-level Magnus-adjacent cultists/Returned, the friend themselves (glimpsed, not yet freed).
- **Goal:** find where Magnus is keeping the friend, hidden from scrying.
- **Complications:** following the trail puts the crew **back on Magnus's radar** (and he wants Arjun); the friend may be changed / not want rescue / be bait; the lead overlaps Netherese sites, seeding **Chapter 3**.

> **Lurking complication (can intrude on any path):** **[[Characters/Demos Twice-Fallen|Demos]]** and the grieving Returned come looking for the crew that baited Ressik — they don't yet know Magnus took her *irreversibly*, and learning it could turn them from accusers into desperate allies.
